prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render. Image 1 is the AUTHORITATIVE WHOLE-BODY MOTION BLUEPRINT: its exact twelve complete poses and phase order must be preserved. Image 2 is CHARACTER DESIGN AND TRAILING KATANA GRIP reference only. Render image1 as twelve complete drawings of image2's white-haired black/red swordsman. Do not copy image2's running leg pose.
Exact layout four columns three rows, 2560x1440 native transparent PNG. Each 640x480 cell uses blueprint joints/foot coordinates. Retain SAME SCALE and cell placement. No titles, text, lines, colored joint circles or guide visible in finished art. Entire bodies and blades comfortably fit cells. Clean simple colored animation pencil-test, reduced costume detail is okay. Adult compact head and long legs, approximate head height58 and neutral-standing380 in requested native pixels. NOT chibi.
Most important: TRACE THE TWELVE DISTINCT WHOLE-BODY POSES of image1, including tightly bent knees and heels lifting toward buttocks, AND THE NEAR/FAR LEG OCCLUSION ORDER. The orange leg in blueprint is always the camera-near RIGHT leg (render normal black pants bright metal armor), blue is always far LEFT leg (render darker black pants dark metal armor). Orange and blue are guidance only, not costume colors. They are distinct legs moving on different continuous paths: near foot grounds and moves backward through frames1-5 while far folded leg swings past it; far foot grounds frames7-11 while near leg swings past. In frames3 and9 the legs are CLOSE TOGETHER AT PASSING, NOT wide stride. In frames4 and10 the swinging knee is forward at hip height, heel tightly folded under the thigh. Frames6 and12 BOTH feet are offground before landing. Do not substitute the same lead-leg pose or rearrange pose order. Render a coherent complete person in each cell, integrate shoulders, torso, hips, head and coat response, never separate limb drawings.
Preserve backwards dragging blade: near right wrapped hand behind hip closes naturally around handle with visible thumb over curled index finger, katana blade extends screenLEFT slightly downward, edgeDOWN. Blade length and hand anatomy identical across sequence. Free arm follows blueprint. Shorten flowing coat silhouette just enough for both knees to remain readable but retain costume identity. Keep weapons and figures isolated without neighboring overlap. No shadow, effects, motion blur, extra figures or source neutral reference figure. This is twelve consecutive instants of ONE connected running person. Geometry from image1 takes precedence over image2's static pose.
